distillation_scope.leaf_granularity: first-layer clinical disease leaf for polymyositis, without adding antisynthetase syndrome, dermatomyositis, inclusion body myositis, immune-mediated necrotizing myopathy, overlap syndrome, trigger, severity, or organ-complication qualifiers to the disease name
distillation_scope.subtype_policy: Trigger context, malignancy context, viral/post-infectious context, connective-tissue-disease overlap context, ILD, myocarditis, rhabdomyolysis, and treatment-refractory course are represented as mechanisms, axes, risk factors, event hazards, and treatment modifiers. Closely related myositis subtypes and mimics can become separate leaves later.
distillation_scope.ranking_note: Presentation ranking may use observed proximal weakness, myalgia, dysphagia, respiratory muscle weakness, CK/myoglobin/LDH/transaminases, inflammatory markers, renal injury from rhabdomyolysis, and presentation imaging when available. Muscle biopsy, EMG, myositis antibodies, final paper diagnosis, and treatment response should be confirmatory or non-ranking unless a post-workup mode explicitly consumes them.

latent_mechanisms.clinical_meaning: Immune-mediated endomysial inflammation and myofiber injury drive the core polymyositis muscle manifold.

latent_mechanisms.display_name: Myofiber necrosis, regeneration, and enzyme leakage
latent_mechanisms.clinical_meaning: Active myofiber injury leaks CK, myoglobin, LDH, AST, and ALT and can progress to rhabdomyolysis.

latent_mechanisms.display_name: Proximal, bulbar, and respiratory muscle weakness
latent_mechanisms.clinical_meaning: Inflammatory muscle dysfunction causes shoulder/hip girdle weakness, neck flexor weakness, dysphagia, impaired mobility, and occasionally respiratory muscle failure.
Cytokine and acute-phase activity can produce fatigue, fever, CRP/ESR elevation, anemia of inflammation, thrombocytosis, hypoalbuminemia, and weight loss.
A subset of polymyositis courses involve ILD, myocarditis, arrhythmia, or other organ-level inflammatory complications.

latent_mechanisms.display_name: Rhabdomyolysis and myoglobinuric kidney injury pathway
latent_mechanisms.clinical_meaning: Very high myofiber injury can create myoglobinuria, oliguria, creatinine/BUN rise, and acute kidney injury hazard.

mechanism_edges.clinical_rationale: Endomysial immune injury damages myofibers and raises muscle enzymes.
Inflamed proximal and axial muscles lose strength over days to months.
Active autoimmune myositis can generate systemic acute-phase activity.
Extreme muscle breakdown can become rhabdomyolysis with renal tubular injury.
Active inflammatory myositis can produce MRI muscle edema.
Needle EMG can show irritable myopathy with fibrillations and short-duration polyphasic motor units.
Some active polymyositis cases show increased radionuclide uptake in inflamed muscles.
Symmetric proximal weakness is the dominant clinical expression of polymyositis.
Neck flexors can be involved with axial myositis.
Difficulty rising, walking, lifting arms, dressing, or standing tracks weakness burden.
Bulbar or esophageal involvement can cause dysphagia and aspiration risk.
Severe axial or diaphragmatic weakness can impair ventilation.
Muscle pain or tenderness may accompany inflammatory muscle injury.
CK is the main muscle injury enzyme axis in polymyositis.
Aldolase may rise with muscle injury even when CK is less informative.
Myoglobin rises with muscle breakdown and contributes to renal injury risk.
LDH commonly rises with muscle injury.
AST can rise from skeletal muscle injury.
ALT may rise with myositis or concurrent hepatic stress, usually less specifically than AST/CK.
Marked muscle enzyme release, myoglobinuria, and dark urine indicate rhabdomyolysis.
Myoglobinuric tubular injury may reduce urine output.
Rhabdomyolysis-associated AKI can raise serum creatinine.
Rhabdomyolysis-associated AKI can raise BUN.
Myoglobinuric tubular injury raises AKI event hazard.
Fatigue and malaise track systemic inflammation and muscle disease burden.
Chronic inflammation and dysphagia can cause weight loss.
Fever can occur but is not required and should not suppress infectious mimics.
CRP can be elevated with systemic inflammatory myositis.
ESR may rise with inflammatory myopathy.
Leukocytosis can accompany inflammation, stress, steroids, or infection mimics.
Reactive thrombocytosis may track acute-phase inflammation.
Anemia of inflammation can accompany chronic active disease.
Inflammation, catabolism, poor intake, and severe illness can lower albumin.
Dyspnea can arise from respiratory muscle weakness or ILD.
Polymyositis can have ILD, though this should remain separable from antisynthetase syndrome context.
ILD or respiratory muscle weakness can lower oxygenation.
Inflammatory myopathy can rarely involve myocardium.
Myocardial involvement can produce arrhythmia risk.
Dysphagia and secretion mismanagement increase aspiration pneumonia risk.
Respiratory muscle weakness can progress to ventilatory failure.
Aspiration pneumonia can precipitate hypoxemia and respiratory failure.
Respiratory failure is a major short-term death pathway in severe polymyositis.
Severe AKI from rhabdomyolysis increases mortality and need for organ support.
Myocarditis can raise death risk through heart failure or arrhythmia.
Clinically important arrhythmia can acutely raise mortality.
Most polymyositis is not immediately fatal, but severe systemic inflammation and complications increase hazard.

axes.shape_free_text: Symmetric shoulder and hip girdle weakness, difficulty rising, climbing stairs, lifting arms, combing hair, dressing, or walking.
Neck flexor weakness from axial myositis.
Functional disability caused by myositis weakness, from difficulty with activities to inability to stand or walk unaided.
Muscle pain, tenderness, or body aches associated with inflammatory myopathy.
Oropharyngeal or esophageal swallowing impairment from inflammatory myopathy.
Respiratory muscle weakness, hypoventilation, or difficulty clearing secretions caused by myositis.
Fatigue or malaise accompanying active myositis.
Weight loss from chronic inflammation, dysphagia, or severe illness.
MRI edema or inflammatory signal in proximal or involved skeletal muscles.
Needle EMG pattern compatible with active irritable myopathy.
Increased radionuclide bone-scan uptake in multiple inflamed skeletal muscles.
CK elevation from inflammatory myofiber injury; can be mild in chronic treated disease or extreme with rhabdomyolysis.
Aldolase elevation from muscle injury.
Myoglobin release from muscle breakdown.
LDH elevation from skeletal muscle injury or severe systemic illness.
AST elevation from muscle injury; may exceed ALT when muscle dominates.
ALT can rise during myositis or concurrent hepatic stress.
Clinical rhabdomyolysis activity, such as extreme CK, myoglobinuria, dark urine, and severe muscle breakdown.
CRP may be normal, modestly elevated, or very high in severe inflammatory or complication-rich polymyositis; infection remains a key mimic.
ESR elevation from systemic inflammation.
Fever is optional in polymyositis and high fever should keep infection and systemic inflammatory mimics competitive.
Tachycardia may follow inflammation, pain, anemia, infection, or cardiac involvement.
White blood cell count is often normal but can rise with stress, inflammation, steroids, infection, or malignancy context.
Reactive thrombocytosis can accompany acute-phase inflammation.
Hemoglobin may be low from chronic inflammation, malignancy, kidney disease, or unrelated comorbidity.
Hypoalbuminemia can reflect inflammation, poor intake, dysphagia, malignancy, renal disease, or severe illness.
Reduced urine output during rhabdomyolysis-associated kidney injury.
Creatinine can rise when polymyositis is complicated by rhabdomyolysis-associated acute kidney injury; background kidney disease must be handled as patient context.
BUN can rise with severe renal complication, dehydration, catabolism, or background kidney disease.
Dyspnea from respiratory muscle weakness, ILD, cardiac involvement, anemia, or mimic disease.
ILD extent when polymyositis has pulmonary involvement; antisynthetase syndrome remains a separate context/mimic.
Oxygen saturation may fall with severe ILD, aspiration, respiratory muscle failure, or unrelated cardiopulmonary disease.
Aspiration event hazard from dysphagia and secretion mismanagement.
Respiratory failure hazard from respiratory muscle weakness, ILD, or aspiration complications.
AKI hazard from rhabdomyolysis, myoglobinuria, dehydration, or severe illness.
Myocarditis hazard in rare cardiac polymyositis involvement.
Arrhythmia hazard when cardiac inflammation or severe systemic illness is present.
Serious infection hazard from high-dose immunosuppression, immobility, aspiration, lines, or background frailty.
Lifespan outcome hazard for polymyositis, driven mainly by respiratory failure, aspiration, severe renal injury, cardiac involvement, infection, malignancy context, and frailty.

axis_couplings.clinical_rationale: Dysphagia and secretion mismanagement raise aspiration pneumonia risk.
Respiratory muscle weakness can directly increase respiratory failure hazard.
Hypoxemia indicates higher respiratory failure hazard.
Extreme CK can mark rhabdomyolysis severity and AKI risk.
CK and weakness often move together through active myositis, but either can be discordant.
Aspiration pneumonia can progress to respiratory failure.
Respiratory failure is a major near-term mortality pathway.
Severe AKI increases mortality and organ-support need.
Infection after aspiration, lines, or immunosuppression can dominate mortality risk.

treatments.clinical_role: Rapidly suppresses autoimmune muscle and systemic inflammatory activity.

trajectory_modifications.clinical_rationale: Glucocorticoids rapidly reduce inflammatory myositis activity.
Glucocorticoids reduce acute-phase inflammation.
High-dose steroids increase infection risk, especially in frail or aspirating patients.

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: Active or probable infection can change the net vector field of immunosuppression.
Diabetes or severe illness increases steroid hyperglycemia toxicity.

treatments.clinical_role: Disease-modifying steroid-sparing control for sustained polymyositis activity.

trajectory_modifications.clinical_rationale: Conventional immunosuppression reduces chronic T-cell-mediated myositis activity.
As muscle inflammation improves, CK tends to fall.

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: Renal dysfunction can limit methotrexate use and increase cytopenia or mucosal toxicity.
Significant liver injury changes the safety of hepatotoxic steroid-sparing agents.

treatments.clinical_role: Steroid-sparing immune control, especially when lung involvement or methotrexate constraints exist.

trajectory_modifications.clinical_rationale: Mycophenolate dampens lymphocyte proliferation.
May reduce inflammatory lung involvement in selected myositis contexts.

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: Additional immunosuppression can worsen infection risk.

treatments.clinical_role: Immune modulation for severe, refractory, dysphagic, or rapidly progressive polymyositis.

trajectory_modifications.clinical_rationale: Immunoglobulin can improve refractory inflammatory myositis.
Dysphagia can improve when myositis activity falls.

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: Renal impairment and volume/osmotic load shape immunoglobulin safety.
Immunoglobulin can increase thrombotic risk in susceptible patients.

treatments.clinical_role: Escalation immune modulation for refractory or severe disease after standard agents are insufficient.

trajectory_modifications.clinical_rationale: B-cell depletion can help selected refractory inflammatory myopathy courses.
B-cell depletion increases infection and viral reactivation risk.

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: HBV reactivation risk must be managed before anti-CD20 therapy.

treatments.clinical_role: Escalation for severe organ-threatening ILD, myocarditis, or rapidly progressive refractory myositis.

trajectory_modifications.clinical_rationale: Alkylating immunosuppression can suppress severe inflammatory organ involvement.
Cyclophosphamide increases cytopenia and infection hazard.

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: Baseline cytopenia or marrow compromise limits cytotoxic therapy.

treatments.display_name: Tacrolimus or cyclosporine for refractory or lung context
treatments.clinical_role: Additional immune suppression for refractory disease or lung-dominant myositis contexts.

trajectory_modifications.clinical_rationale: Calcineurin inhibition reduces T-cell activation.

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: Nephrotoxicity risk limits calcineurin inhibitor use in AKI or CKD.

treatments.clinical_role: Reduces aspiration and nutritional harm while immunosuppression takes effect.

trajectory_modifications.clinical_rationale: Diet modification, speech therapy, secretion management, and enteral feeding reduce aspiration risk.
Nutritional support can improve intake-related hypoalbuminemia over time.

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: This support matters most when dysphagia is active.

treatments.clinical_role: Supports oxygenation and ventilation during respiratory muscle weakness, aspiration, or ILD.

trajectory_modifications.clinical_rationale: Supplemental oxygen or ventilatory support directly improves oxygenation.
Ventilatory support reduces immediate failure risk but does not stop autoimmune myositis.

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: Respiratory support has its main survival effect when respiratory failure risk is active.

treatments.clinical_role: Hydration, electrolyte management, and renal replacement support when severe rhabdomyolysis or AKI is active.

trajectory_modifications.clinical_rationale: Supportive renal care reduces immediate kidney-injury consequences.
Managing severe renal complications can reduce short-term mortality.

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: Renal support is outcome-relevant when AKI risk is active.

treatments.clinical_role: Restores function and prevents deconditioning after inflammatory activity is controlled enough for safe exercise.

trajectory_modifications.clinical_rationale: Physical therapy improves function and reduces deconditioning.

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: Aggressive exercise during uncontrolled rhabdomyolysis or severe weakness can be unsafe.

present.clinical_rationale: Adult onset is typical, and older age reduces reserve during complications.
Polymyositis is more common in women, although men can be affected.
Cancer can be a contextual trigger or competing driver of inflammatory myopathy severity and poor reserve.
Post-infectious immune activation can temporally precede polymyositis, while acute infection remains a mimic.
Sjögren, RA, SLE, systemic sclerosis, and other connective-tissue disease contexts can coexist with inflammatory myopathy; overlap should not be baked into the disease name.
Bulbar involvement changes complication and mortality trajectory.
Pulmonary or ventilatory involvement is a major severity modifier.
Myocarditis or arrhythmia context raises complication hazard.
Background kidney disease changes base measures and worsens tolerance of rhabdomyolysis and treatment.
Diabetes and frailty increase glucocorticoid infection and metabolic toxicity.
Immunosuppression can mute or distort inflammation while raising infection hazard.

supportive_care.clinical_role: Actively evaluate dermatomyositis, antisynthetase syndrome, inclusion body myositis, immune-mediated necrotizing myopathy, muscular dystrophy, endocrine or metabolic myopathy, drug-induced myopathy, infection, malignancy, neuropathy, myasthenia, and motor neuron disease without encoding any of them into the polymyositis disease name.

Use observed symptoms, labs, vitals, and presentation imaging for presentation ranking; keep muscle biopsy, EMG, myositis antibodies, final diagnosis, and treatment response as confirmatory unless the workflow is explicitly post-workup.
Track swallowing safety, secretion management, oxygenation, respiratory mechanics, ECG/troponin/echo when indicated, and aspiration or ventilatory failure risk.
Trend CK, aldolase or LDH, AST/ALT, myoglobin when available, urinalysis/dark urine, creatinine, BUN, electrolytes, and urine output during severe myofiber injury.
Assess malignancy and connective tissue disease context as modifiers rather than disease-name qualifiers.
Provide graded rehabilitation, mobility aids, fall prevention, nutrition, bone protection, and steroid-toxicity monitoring.

quality_notes: The disease prompt scope is pure disease name: Polymyositis.
The only derived_hazard axis is mortality_hazard_in_D-POLYMYOSITIS.
No first-line, preferred, guideline-recommended, indication-strength, diagnosis-should-be, or hard ranking fields are used.
